## Objective
Write the complete test suite for a dependency-free browser Snake game, before any implementation exists. The suite uses only `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`. Later tasks implement `src/game.js` (T2) and `src/controls.js`, `src/main.js`, `index.html`, `src/style.css` (T3) and are graded by these files, so they must be precise and must not depend on unspecified implementation details. The tests are expected to fail right now because the stubs throw `not implemented` and `src/main.js` and `index.html` do not exist.

## Interface
Read `src/game.js` (types `GameState`, `Point`, `Direction`, `Status`; functions `createGame`, `placeFood`, `setDirection`, `step`, `tickInterval`; constants `DEFAULT_WIDTH`, `DEFAULT_HEIGHT`, `INITIAL_LENGTH`, `DIRECTIONS`) and `src/controls.js` (`keyToDirection`, `keyToCommand`). Files to create, all ES modules importing with relative paths such as `../src/game.js`:
- `test/game.test.js` imports from `../src/game.js`.
- `test/controls.test.js` imports from `../src/controls.js`.
- `test/main.test.js` loads `../src/main.js` with a fake DOM (see Behavior 3).
- `test/ui.test.js` reads `index.html`, `src/main.js`, `src/style.css` as text with `node:fs`.
The tests run with `node --test test/` from the repository root.

## Behavior
Required game semantics (the contract the tests encode):
- Board coordinates: x grows right, y grows down, origin top-left. Snake `snake[0]` is the head.
- `createGame()` defaults to a 20 by 20 board, snake `[{x:10,y:10},{x:9,y:10},{x:8,y:10}]`, `direction` and `nextDirection` both `'right'`, score 0, status `'running'`, and a food point that is in bounds and not on the snake. For `{width:8,height:6}` the head is `{x:4,y:3}`. It throws `RangeError` when width or height is below 5 or not an integer.
- `placeFood(width, height, snake, rng)` enumerates free cells row by row (y outer loop, x inner loop), picks index `Math.floor(rng() * freeCount)` clamped to the last index, and returns `null` when no cell is free.
- `setDirection` returns a state whose `nextDirection` is the requested direction, except it returns the state unchanged when the status is not `'running'`, the direction is not one of the four names, or the direction is the opposite of `state.direction` (the last applied move, not the queued one).
- `step(state, rng)` returns a new state without mutating the input. A non-running state is returned as the same reference. Otherwise it applies `nextDirection` to `direction`, moves the head one cell, and: leaving the board gives status `'over'` with the snake unchanged; entering a body cell gives `'over'`, except that entering the cell the tail is vacating is legal when no food is eaten; eating food keeps the tail (snake grows by one), adds 1 to score, and places new food through `placeFood` using `rng`; when `placeFood` returns `null` the status becomes `'won'` and food is `null`.
- `tickInterval(score)` equals `Math.max(70, 150 - 5 * score)`.

Test cases to write:
1. `test/game.test.js`, grouped with `describe` or flat `test` calls:
   a. createGame defaults, custom size, the RangeError cases, and `rng: () => 0` putting food at the first free cell in row order, which is `{x:0,y:0}` on a default board.
   b. placeFood: `rng: () => 0` gives the first free cell; `rng: () => 0.999999` gives the last free cell; cells covered by the snake are never returned (width 3, height 1, snake on x=0 and x=1 returns `{x:2,y:0}`); a 2 by 2 board fully covered by the snake returns `null`.
   c. step basics: from the default state one step moves the head to `{x:11,y:10}`, keeps length 3, and leaves the input object deep-equal to a `structuredClone` taken before the call. After `setDirection(state,'up')` a step gives head `{x:10,y:9}` and `direction` `'up'`.
   d. setDirection: reversal ignored; a second call that is opposite to `direction` but not to the queued value is ignored (state moving right, queue `'up'`, then `'left'` leaves `nextDirection` as `'up'`); invalid values (`'diagonal'`, `undefined`) ignored; ignored when status is `'over'`.
   e. Eating: build a hand-made state (spread of `createGame({rng: () => 0})` with `food` set to `{x:11,y:10}`); `step(state, () => 0)` yields length 4, score 1, and a new food that is not on the snake.
   f. Collisions: wall hit on each of the four sides using hand-made states of a 20 by 20 board; self hit using snake `[{x:5,y:5},{x:6,y:5},{x:6,y:6},{x:5,y:6},{x:4,y:6}]` with `direction` `'left'` and `nextDirection` `'down'` giving `'over'`; the vacating-tail case using snake `[{x:5,y:5},{x:6,y:5},{x:6,y:6},{x:5,y:6}]` with `direction` `'left'`, `nextDirection` `'down'`, food elsewhere, giving status `'running'` and head `{x:5,y:6}`.
   g. A `'over'` state stepped again returns the identical object (`assert.equal` on references).
   h. Win: width 3, height 1, snake `[{x:1,y:0},{x:0,y:0}]`, both directions `'right'`, food `{x:2,y:0}`; one step gives status `'won'`, food `null`, score 1, length 3.
   i. tickInterval values: 150 at score 0, 140 at score 2, 70 at score 100, and 70 at score 1000.
2. `test/controls.test.js`: `keyToDirection` maps `ArrowUp`/`w`/`W` to up, `ArrowDown`/`s`/`S` to down, `ArrowLeft`/`a`/`A` to left, `ArrowRight`/`d`/`D` to right, and returns `null` for `'x'`, `' '`, `''`. `keyToCommand` maps `' '`, `'p'`, `'P'` to `'pause'`; `'r'`, `'R'`, `'Enter'` to `'restart'`; `null` for `'x'` and `'ArrowUp'`.
3. `test/main.test.js` tests `src/main.js` against a fake DOM. A helper `load(t)` must, for every test: call `t.mock.timers.enable({ apis: ['setTimeout'] })`; build `globalThis.document` with `getElementById(id)` returning fake elements for `'board'`, `'score'`, `'message'`, and `addEventListener(type, fn)` recording handlers; the board is `{ width: 480, height: 480, getContext: () => ctx }` where `ctx` is a `Proxy` that accepts any method call by pushing the method name onto a `calls` array and accepts any property assignment; `score` and `message` are `{ textContent: '' }`. Then import the module with a unique query string so each test gets a fresh instance: `await import('../src/main.js?case=' + counter++)`. A `press(key)` helper calls the recorded `keydown` handler with `{ key, preventDefault() }` that counts calls. Delete `globalThis.document` in `t.after`. Cases:
   a. After load the canvas was drawn (`calls.length > 0`), `message.textContent` matches `/start/i`, `score.textContent` matches `/0/`, and advancing the mock clock by 5000 ms in steps of 200 draws nothing more.
   b. `press('ArrowRight')` calls preventDefault, empties `message.textContent`, and advancing the clock by 200 ms increases `calls.length`.
   c. While running, `press(' ')` makes `message.textContent` match `/paused/i`, and further clock advances add no draw calls; pressing `' '` again empties the message and ticks draw again.
   d. Starting with `ArrowRight` and advancing the clock by 200 ms twenty times ends with `message.textContent` matching `/game over/i` (the head reaches the right wall after ten steps), and further clock advances add no draw calls.
   e. After game over, `press('Enter')` leaves a message that does not match `/game over/i`, `score.textContent` matching `/0/`, and ticks draw again; the same holds when `press(' ')` is used instead of Enter.
   f. A key such as `'x'` does not call preventDefault and draws nothing.
4. `test/ui.test.js`: `index.html` exists and contains a `<canvas` element with `id="board"`, elements with `id="score"` and `id="message"`, `<script type="module" src="src/main.js">` and `<link rel="stylesheet" href="src/style.css">`; `src/main.js` and `src/style.css` exist; `src/main.js` contains import specifiers `./game.js` and `./controls.js` and the string `keydown`, and every relative import specifier in it resolves to an existing file.

## Invariants
- Only `node:test`, `node:assert/strict`, `node:fs` and `node:path`/`node:url` are used; no npm packages, no network.
- Tests are deterministic: always inject `rng`, never rely on `Math.random`, wall-clock time or real timers.
- Do not create or modify anything outside the four listed test files. Do not edit `src/game.js` or `src/controls.js`.

## Edge cases
- `test/main.test.js` must restore globals so one test cannot leak a fake `document` into another.
- Hand-made states must contain every `GameState` field (`width`, `height`, `snake`, `direction`, `nextDirection`, `food`, `score`, `status`).
- Use `assert.deepEqual` from `node:assert/strict` (strict comparison) for points and arrays.

## Guardrails
- Do not weaken a case to make it pass against the stubs; the stubs are supposed to fail.
- Do not run `npm test` expecting green; the only check for this task is that every test file parses (`node --check`).
- `package.json` already sets `"type": "module"`; use `import`, not `require`.

## Out of scope
Implementing any source file, styling checks, pixel-level canvas assertions, touch controls, and high-score persistence.
